candidates.headline: Anthropic employees put $372,000 into an Alaska governor candidate who wants to freeze every new data center in the state
candidates.verdict: DECLINED ON CONFLICT OF INTEREST, not on merit
candidates.merit: On the facts this is the strongest Alaska-AI story of the window: multi-sourced across ADN, Alaska Public Media and The Alaska Story, with a signed first-person ADN op-ed from the $100,000 donor confirming his own gift and motive, and a named state-level AI and data-center policy platform.
candidates.why_declined: This Dispatch is written and voiced by an Anthropic model. A piece in which that automation takes a position on Anthropic employees' political donations, and on AI regulation those donations fund, cannot meet this channel's own honesty standard without a disclosure the video format cannot carry credibly. The conflict is structural, not a matter of careful wording. ESCALATED TO THE OWNER in the Gmail draft instead, with sources, so a human can decide whether and how Alaska.Ai covers it. Recording it here so a future run does not mistake this for a story nobody found.

candidates.headline: More than 50 of Alaska's automated aviation weather stations went dark at once, about a third of the network
candidates.notes: 2026-07-27 outage, reported 07-28 and 07-29. Honest AI angle is the observation layer every forecast model infers from, and no AI failed. Sourcing caveat: one reporter (Alena Naiden) carried by three outlets in one public-media network, so it is ONE sourcing chain, strengthened by two named experts with different institutional interests (UAF's Rick Thoman, Airmen's Association's Adam White). Cause still officially unconfirmed.
candidates.corroboration: Independently surfaced by a SECOND beat (energy/defense/aviation) which read the KTOO copy in full and confirmed the same figures: 50-plus stations down 2026-07-27, about 20 still down that afternoon, up to 20 offline on a NORMAL day per UAF's Rick Thoman, which reframes it as a chronic condition rather than a one-off. Stations are mostly FAA-owned with some NWS and DoD. Still ONE reporter (Alena Naiden) and one origin story carried by KNBA and KTOO. No FAA statement on cause, so no cause may be asserted on screen.

candidates.headline: A grey box on the Wood River launches a drone at 8:30 every morning, and a computer-vision model is learning to count Bristol Bay sockeye
candidates.verdict: REJECTED on SHAPE REPEAT, after an honest dedupe re-test
candidates.merit: Genuinely strong: real supervised computer vision, regional funders (BBRSDA, BBEDC, UW Fisheries Research Institute), named people (Norm Van Vactor, Joel Tibbs, Ian Chiu), and a superb drawable contrast between a solar-powered box that opens at 8:30 a.m. and a human in a wooden tower hand-clicking salmon for ten minutes of every hour, a method unchanged since 1955.
candidates.dedupe_reasoning: scripts/dedupe.py returned DUP against the 07-24 Quinhagak dispatch on ['bay','box','drone','river'] and against 07-23 on ['counts','vision']. Those are GENERIC TOKENS and per the routine a token collision must not kill a distinct subject, so I re-tested with an honest distinctive entity set. The script still only token-matches and cannot answer the real question, so I applied the viewer's test directly. THE ANSWER IS THAT THIS IS A REPEAT, on story SHAPE rather than tokens. The channel has already shipped two dispatches in the last nine days with this exact shape: 07-21 'The Referee Arrives' (NOAA AFSC YOLOv11 counting salmon in trawl net-cam footage, expert annotation, research not deployed) and 07-23 'Counting Belugas From Orbit' (NOAA/USGS GAIA machine vision counting Cook Inlet belugas, expert annotation, experimental not deployed). A third experimental-computer-vision-model-in-training-counts-Alaska-fauna film, and the SECOND about counting salmon specifically, is a story a regular viewer would feel they had already been shown. Noting explicitly that this is the OPPOSITE error from the 07-29 failure: there a real scoop was killed by a generic token, here the tokens read fresh and the shape does not. Both failures are real and this one is the honest call.
candidates.carried_forward: Strong lead for a LATER dispatch once the model is validated against ADF&G tower counts, which is the genuinely new news and a different story (a thing that WORKS, not a thing in training).
candidates.do_not_air: The snippeted phase-one figures 256 drone flights and 17,552 images are UNVERIFIED (Undercurrent News and SeafoodSource both 403'd). Never air them.
candidates.confidence: high on facts, rejected on freshness-of-shape

candidates.headline: Alaska's tribal health system is writing the rules for medical AI before the vendors arrive, and the test case is the medevac call
candidates.verdict: REJECTED on timeliness, flagged as a strong future subject
candidates.notes: Peer-reviewed symposium report in the International Journal of Circumpolar Health, 31 participants from ANTHC, Southcentral Foundation, Maniilaq Association, Stanford and the CDC Arctic Investigations Program; data sovereignty over AI/ML in the Alaska Tribal Health System; medevac decisions occur roughly 40 times more often than the national rate. The most substantive Alaska AI governance work found on any beat, and genuinely unreported by Alaska outlets. But it published 2026-05-23, which is 68 days old, outside BOTH the 10-day window and the 30-day unreported allowance. The researcher flagged the date honestly rather than burying it. Also: its one candidate quote came back with an ellipsis and is NOT certified verbatim, so it could not be aired as written without a re-read.
candidates.cultural_note: If ever used: ANTHC is a statewide tribal health organization, Southcentral Foundation is the Anchorage-area tribal health organization, Maniilaq Association serves the Northwest Arctic. None speaks for the others and none speaks for Alaska Native people as a bloc. 31 people at one symposium are not a referendum.
candidates.confidence: medium-high on facts, rejected on timeliness

locked_story.headline: Navy asks to run a robot fleet under the ice off Alaska's North Slope for a ninth year, launched from UAF's own research ship
locked_story.primary_source: 91 FR 46055-46079 (doc 2026-14816), NOAA Fisheries proposed incidental harassment authorization, ONR Arctic Research Activities Year 9
why_this_one: Robotics is explicitly in the routine's scope, so autonomy is not a stretch on this beat, it is the beat.
Genuinely unreported. No 2026 coverage of AMOS exists anywhere the researcher could find, and NOAA's own incidental-take index has not listed it yet.
Fresh: eight days old, and the public comment docket is OPEN until 2026-08-21, so the film has real civic utility rather than being a retrospective.
A brand-new visual world for this channel. Every prior dispatch has been above water. This one is under a meter of sea ice, in the dark, navigating by sound.

It fills a real library gap. The shelf holds an orbital eye (SatelliteEye), a seafloor ear (ListeningMooring), a ground ear (SeismicStation) and two aerial machines (Vale, Petrel), but nothing that SWIMS. That justifies the run's net-new asset instead of manufacturing one.

It has an honest two-sided structure without forcing either side: a genuinely impressive engineering answer to a hard problem (an acoustic substitute for GPS where no satellite can reach), and a real open question (Level B harassment authorized on beluga and ringed seal, both subsistence species, with a comment window nobody in Alaska has been told about).
Hero differs from the last two heroes (Sourdough on 07-29, RecordsMachine on 07-26), satisfying the cast-freshness gate.
locked_story.dedupe_record: dedupe.py returned DUP twice on purely generic tokens, ['naval','research'] against the 07-23 beluga satellite dispatch because the Naval Research Laboratory was a GAIA partner, and ['2026','year'] against 07-25. Both were re-tested with honest distinctive entity sets and the subject is unrelated in each case. With the hero declared the gate returns FRESH. This is exactly the generic-token trap that killed a real scoop on 07-29, and it was not repeated here.
hard_constraints: Cause of nothing may be asserted beyond the document. NOAA proposes Level B harassment ONLY, with no serious injury or mortality anticipated; do NOT state a take number, because the researcher did not extract the authorized counts.
This is autonomy and engineering, NOT machine learning. The notice contains no AI. Say so plainly on screen, the way the 07-26 film did.
R/V Sikuliaq is ice-strengthened and explicitly NOT an icebreaker. CGC HEALY is named only as a POSSIBLE recovery vessel and 'icebreaking may be required'. Do not upgrade either claim.
Prior-AMOS performance color from search snippets (367-day missions, 233 consecutive days under ice) is UNVERIFIED and must not be aired.
Inupiat subsistence use of these waters is real and must be framed with respect and specificity, never as a bloc opinion and never with characterized-object humor.
